storylets.speaker: Aldous
storylets.title: The keeper of the friendly light.
pages: This beacon's keeper comes down the lamp stair two at a time when you bang the rail twice: tall, weathered, with the careful hands of a man who trims wicks for a living and the pale eyes of exactly one family on this coast.

'Two bangs,' he says, wonder in it. 'Nobody's rung two bangs on my rail in twenty years. You've been in my brother's shop.' He laughs, and the laugh is Sefton's, escaped from a thinner cage. 'Aldous. The fool sells rope, I stand light, and between us we've not said a word in twenty years over which of us loves the water properly.' He feeds you lamp-room tea, stronger than the Keeper's, which you had not believed possible. 'Tell me everything about the quay. Lie where necessary. Beacon men live on news the way lamps live on oil.'

storylets.speaker: Aldous
storylets.title: Three bangs on the rail.
pages: You bang the rail three times, and the sound is still rolling across the water when the lamp room window flies open above you. Aldous stands frozen in it, a man hit by twenty years arriving all at once.

'Three,' he says, mostly to himself. 'He rang three.' He comes down the stair slowly this time, one step at a time, like a man carrying something full to the brim. At the rail he grips your shoulder hard enough to leave weather of its own. 'The season turns at the spring tide,' he says. 'The relief boat runs that week. Tell the rope-selling old fool,' and his voice does exactly what Sefton's did, breaks in exactly the same place, the way a code shared is a thing shared, 'tell him to put the cribbage board where the customers can't see it. I'll not be beaten at cribbage in PUBLIC.'

storylets.title: The beacon keeper's tale: the lamp that argued.
pages: The keeper of this beacon, against all regulation, keeps two lamps burning: the great one above, and a small brass one in the window of the watch room, and the small one, the keeper swears, is the senior partner. 'Was my predecessor's. The night of the Glass Squall, the records say every light on this coast guttered in the pressure drop, all but the small brass ones, the household lamps, the lamps people lit for SOMEONE rather than for shipping in general.'
The keeper turns the little lamp's wick up a thumb's width, out of respect. 'My theory? The sea can argue with infrastructure. It cannot argue with love. Cup of tea before you go?'

storylets.title: The beacon keeper's tale: the dry shelf.
pages: Inside this beacon, above the tide line of the worst recorded storm, there is a shelf the keepers call the dry shelf, and on it, by tradition older than the beacon's stones, anything the sea returns is kept for one year and a day in case its owner comes asking.

Tonight the dry shelf holds: a child's boot, a fiddle in its case with the strings still true, a photograph of a wedding party on a dock you do not recognize, and a ship's bell, small, brass, green with age, engraved L. JANE. The keeper watches you read it. 'Been there nineteen years,' she says quietly. 'Year and a day came and went, and not one of us had the heart. I'd say it's been waiting, captain.' News travels, even out here. Especially out here. 'Take your bell.'

storylets.title: Lamplight and ledger-talk.
pages: The beacon keeper trades you the customary courtesies of the friendly lights: weather honest and weather suspected, which reaches are paying salvage, which buyer at the quay is weighing light this season. You leave warmer than you came, which is the entire engineering purpose of a friendly beacon, whatever the charts say about navigation.

storylets.speaker: Aldous
storylets.title: A light with a forwarding address.
pages: Aldous keeps his light half the year now and the counter stool the other half, the relief service having discovered, to its astonishment, that the coast's most immovable keeper had become negotiable. The lamp room wall bears the evidence of the new arrangement: a cribbage score, chalked in two hands, running to figures that suggest neither brother has ever once let the other win.

'He posts me the shop news in KNOTS,' Aldous says, aggrieved and delighted, holding up a length of cord worked dense as lace. 'A letter, he calls it. Took me two evenings to read the postscript. The postscript was an insult.' He feeds you the customary tea and, at the rail as you go, ties something small and grey to your jacket, the family trade running in him too, after all. 'Fog offshore by morning,' he says. 'That one's for finding your way to a friendly light. Not that you've ever needed it. Humor a keeper. We like our boats spoken for.'

storylets.title: The beacon keeper's tale: the shelf, lighter.
pages: The dry shelf at this beacon is emptier than the last time anyone looked, and the keeper cannot stop telling the story: they are coming for their things. Since the Squall let out its breath, since the word went down the coast that the ledger was ruled off, the claims have started arriving, a year and a day be hanged. A man came for a sextant his father lost with a schooner. Two sisters came for a doll neither would hold first.

'And the fiddle went home,' the keeper says, with the reverence of a witness. 'Woman my age, up from the south coast on the mail boat. Her grandmother's, off the ferry run, before. She didn't say a word. Opened the case, checked the strings, they've held true nineteen years and we have all decided not to wonder how, and she sat down on the shelf edge and played it, one tune, the whole beacon quiet as a held breath.' The keeper turns up the lamp against the dusk. 'The wedding photograph's claimed too, spoken for by a granddaughter who's coming at the season's turn. The shelf will be bare by winter, first time in beacon memory. We're keeping the gull, though. The Admiral stays. Some things belong to the service.'

storylets.title: Held at the light.
pages: The keeper of this beacon has something for you, held back with the ceremony the friendly lights reserve for the sea's own post: a wax-sealed page, fished from the station's water this week and kept dry against the passing of, the keeper says, exactly the right boat. Word travels between the lights. Everyone knows who the post is really for.

choices.label: Take the page, with thanks to the light.
response: The page goes into your dry locker, and the keeper logs the delivery in the station book with genuine satisfaction: RECEIVED, HELD, HANDED ON. The old custom, working. The kettle goes on to celebrate.
